b1-unit-32.32.1 A geography quiz:
Danny: Welcome back to Gap Year Diaries! Today it's quiz time: South America, land and sea. My contestants are Ana and Bruno. Question one. What's the highest mountain in South America?
Bruno: Easy. Aconcagua, in Argentina.
Danny: Correct! It's almost seven thousand meters high. I saw it from the bus on my trip. Question two. Which river carries the most water in the world?
Ana: The Nile?
Bruno: No, the Nile is longer, I think. It's the Amazon!
Danny: Right, Bruno. The Amazon carries more water than any other river on Earth. Question three. The highest waterfall in the world is in South America. Where is it?
Ana: In Venezuela. It's Angel Falls!
Danny: Well done! The water falls nine hundred and seventy-nine meters. That's higher than the tallest building in the world.
Bruno: Wow. For me, Iguazu is still the most beautiful waterfall I've ever seen.
Danny: Question four. What's the highest mountain in Brazil?
Ana: Pico da Neblina! It's on the border with Venezuela, in the Amazon rainforest.
Danny: Correct, it's about three thousand meters high. Have you ever climbed it?
Ana: No way. The highest place I've ever been to is a hill near my grandmother's old farm!
Danny: Question five. Which is the largest tropical wetland in the world?
Bruno: The Pantanal. My uncle took me there when I was a kid. We saw a jaguar!
Danny: Right again. And the last question. What's the driest non-polar desert in the world?
Ana: The Sahara?
Danny: Sorry, Ana. It's the Atacama, in Chile. Some parts get almost no rain at all.
Bruno: So I won! Three points to two!
Ana: Fine. But wait until we do a quiz about medicine!
Danny: Ha! Thanks for listening, everyone!
